stem:
Chetan examines a rock with several different minerals visible under a magnifying glass. Most rocks are mixtures of minerals. He also studies a native mineral that is a pure element, and another mineral made of more than one element, which is a compound rather than an element.

Which classification is correct?

options.text: The rock is a mixture of minerals; the multi-element mineral is a compound; the native mineral is a pure element, not a compound.
The rock is a compound because several minerals sit together in one solid piece.
The native mineral is a compound because it is found in the Earth with other rocks.
Every mineral is an element, including the mineral made of more than one element.

teacher.key_rationale: Most rocks are mixtures of minerals; multi-element minerals are compounds; native minerals are pure elements. Calling the rock a compound swaps mixture for compound. Treating 'found in Earth' as proof of a compound grabs a surface place cue. Calling every mineral an element drops the multi-element compound case.
